title: xk6-sip: PBX under load
description: Signalling, media and generator health for k6 runs with the xk6-sip extension. Tag runs with --tag testid=... and --tag pbx_version=...

panels.title: CAPS
panels.description: New calls per second (call attempts that got a final answer or were cancelled).

panels.title: Calls in progress
panels.description: Answered calls that have not ended yet: sip_calls answered - ended.

targets.expr: sum(k6_sip_calls_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version", phase="answered"}) - (sum(k6_sip_calls_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version", phase="ended"}) or vector(0))

panels.title: ASR
panels.description: Answer-seizure ratio: answered calls / all call attempts over the window, cancelled included. Depends on the traffic mix: busy and no-answer calls lower it without any fault in the PBX.

panels.title: SEER
panels.description: RFC 6076 Session Establishment Effectiveness Ratio: answered calls plus calls the user declined (480, 486, 600, 603) / all attempts except 3xx. Network and server failures (404, 5xx, timeouts) lower it; user behaviour does not.

targets.expr: (sum(rate(k6_sip_call_results_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version", status=~"200|480|486|600|603"}[$window])) or vector(0)) / sum(rate(k6_sip_call_results_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version", status!~"3.."}[$window]))

panels.title: One-way audio
panels.description: Share of call legs that heard no audio from the other side, over the window. Anything above 0 is a real user-facing problem.

panels.title: Dropped iterations
panels.description: Iterations k6 could not start in time (not enough VUs). Above 0 means the generator, not the PBX, is the limit.

panels.title: Setup time p95
panels.description: INVITE sent to final response, 95th percentile over the window.

panels.title: Setup within SLA
panels.description: Share of answered calls set up faster than the SLA variable sla_setup (seconds, top of the dashboard), over the window.

panels.title: PDD within SLA
panels.description: Share of calls whose post-dial delay (INVITE to first 18x) is below the SLA variable sla_pdd (seconds), over the window.

panels.title: ALOC
panels.description: Average length of conversation over the window. A drop at constant load means the PBX cuts calls.

panels.title: First response p95
panels.description: INVITE sent to its first response (usually 100 Trying), 95th percentile. Above T1 = 500 ms the INVITE gets retransmitted.

panels.title: Retransmissions
panels.description: SIP messages sent again per second because the peer did not answer or acknowledge them in time. Above 0 under load is an early sign of overload.

panels.title: Signalling — does the PBX connect calls, and how fast
Calls per second by final status
panels.description: Final INVITE status of each call. A spike of 480/486/503 shows up as a new colour.

panels.title: Call setup time
panels.description: INVITE sent to final response. Dashed line: 300 ms threshold used in the examples.

panels.title: Post-dial delay
panels.description: INVITE sent to the first 18x: how long the caller waits before hearing ringback.

panels.title: INVITE routing time
panels.description: Caller device sending INVITE to callee device receiving it: time spent inside the PBX. Only reported when expectCall() names the caller device.

panels.title: Failed calls by status
panels.description: Failed calls over the selected time range, by final INVITE status.

panels.title: INVITE first response time
panels.description: INVITE sent to its first response, usually 100 Trying. Until it arrives the transaction layer retransmits the INVITE every T1 = 500 ms (dashed line), doubling. A p95 near the line means the PBX is too slow to even acknowledge calls.

panels.title: SIP retransmissions
panels.description: Messages sent again by the transaction layer per second: requests the peer did not answer (INVITE, BYE, REGISTER...) and final responses it did not acknowledge. Retransmissions add load to an already slow PBX; growth under load is an early sign of an overload collapse.

panels.title: Calls per second by response class
panels.description: Final INVITE responses grouped by class. 5xx means the server failed; 4xx is mostly the user or routing (busy, not found, unavailable).

panels.title: Media — do people hear each other
One-way audio
panels.description: Share of call legs without audio from the other side. Signalling says the call succeeded, the person hears nothing.

panels.title: Jitter p95 by leg
panels.description: RFC 3550 interarrival jitter, 95th percentile. out = caller's leg, in = callee's leg.

panels.title: RTP packet loss
panels.description: Lost packets / (received + lost), from RTP sequence numbers.

panels.title: RTP packets per second
panels.description: Sent vs received. RTP counters are reported when a call ends, so the curve is smoothed over the window.

panels.title: Registrations and requests — does the registrar keep up
Registrations (cumulative)
panels.description: REGISTER responses since the start of the run, by status, and the cumulative p95 of successful REGISTERs (right axis). Registrations come in a burst at start and on refresh, so cumulative values read better than rates.

panels.title: Failed requests by method
panels.description: Share of requests that failed (no response, 3xx-6xx). 401/407 auth challenges are not failures.

targets.expr: (sum by (method) (rate(k6_sip_requests_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version", status!~"1..|2..|401|407"}[$window])) or 0 * sum by (method) (rate(k6_sip_requests_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version"}[$window]))) / sum by (method) (rate(k6_sip_requests_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version"}[$window]))

panels.title: Scenario — what went wrong from the test's point of view
Failed expectations
panels.description: expect* calls that returned false. call = no call or wrong caller number, heard = no audio, transferred = transfer failed.

panels.title: Calls ending per second, by who hung up
panels.description: local = the script, remote = the other side or the PBX, timeout, error. A growing remote/error share means the PBX drops calls.

panels.title: Generator health — is it the PBX or the test rig
VUs and calls in progress
panels.description: VUs running vs answered calls in progress.

targets.expr: sum(k6_sip_calls_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version", phase="answered"}) - (sum(k6_sip_calls_total{testid=~"$testid", pbx_version=~"$pbx_version", phase="ended"}) or vector(0))

panels.title: Dropped iterations
panels.description: Iterations k6 skipped because no VU was free. With arrival-rate executors this means preAllocatedVUs is too low.

panels.title: Iteration duration
panels.description: How long one scenario iteration takes, p50 and p95.

panels.title: Machine CPU
panels.description: CPU utilisation of the load generator machine, all cores. From windows_exporter or node-exporter (job=host).

panels.title: Machine memory
panels.description: Physical memory of the load generator machine: used and total.

panels.title: Machine network
panels.description: Traffic of the machine's network interfaces. Loopback traffic (a PBX on the same machine) does not appear here; the k6 process panel counts it.

panels.title: k6 process CPU
panels.description: CPU used by the k6 process; 100% = one full core. Goroutines on the right axis.

panels.title: k6 process memory
panels.description: Resident memory of the k6 process and the Go heap in use. A steady climb over a long run is a leak in the generator, not in the PBX.

panels.title: k6 process network
panels.description: UDP payload on all SIP and RTP sockets of the k6 process, by protocol and direction. Loopback traffic included.
